items.title: New York court recognizes an English divorce but defers recognition of its still-contested financial order
items.publisher: New York State Law Reporting Bureau
items.summary: New York Supreme Court held that an English decree dissolving a marriage qualified for recognition under comity, but denied without prejudice a request to recognize a related financial-remedy order. The latter remained enforceable in England, yet competing applications to vary its child-maintenance and security provisions were set for imminent hearing there. With no arrears or present enforcement request in New York, the court treated temporary deferral—not lack of foreign finality—as the appropriate result.

items.title: ATF finalizes two Safe Explosives Act rules after twenty-three years
items.publisher: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives
items.summary: ATF converts two 2003 interim rules into a final rule effective October 26. The agency clarifies that explosives licensees and permittees must report added or removed responsible persons and authorized employees within 30 days, while eliminating identity-verification duties for people accepting carrier deliveries on a buyer’s behalf. It also rescinds a 2003 variance that had supplied an alternative procedure. The unusually long interim period makes the rule a case study in deferred administrative finalization.

items.title: Transportation Department replaces group presumptions with individual disadvantage findings
items.summary: The Transportation Department finalizes its 2025 interim revision of the Disadvantaged Business Enterprise and Airport Concession Disadvantaged Business Enterprise programs. Race- and sex-based presumptions are removed; every participating firm must instead establish disadvantaged ownership through an individualized personal narrative. DOT says the prior presumptions were unconstitutional and that this rule makes only administrative refinements, including clearer comparison language and reevaluation deadlines, after considering 637 public comments. The rule takes effect immediately.

items.title: EPA limits when Title V permits can reopen earlier air-pollution decisions
items.summary: EPA’s final rule states that Clean Air Act Title V operating-permit review generally may not be used to relitigate requirements fixed in New Source Review permits issued with notice and judicial-review opportunities. EPA identifies narrow exceptions where construction requirements were never conclusively established or materially overlap with Title V issues. It also excludes the hazardous-substance accidental-release general duty from Title V’s “applicable requirements.” The agency says the rule codifies existing policy and resolves conflicting appellate approaches.

items.title: Census releases an annual inventory of U.S. state and local government units
items.summary: The Census Bureau released its 2026 Annual Government Organization tables and public-use file. The publication identifies government units by state, separates local governments by type, and classifies special districts by function; the downloadable file also describes dependent school systems and public pension systems. These data provide the federal government’s official organizational count between the quinquennial Census of Governments, making otherwise diffuse public institutions available for comparisons of fragmentation, service delivery, and fiscal structure.

items.title: HUD puts eleven defaulted healthcare-property mortgages up for sealed bidding
items.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
items.summary: HUD will auction eleven unsubsidized, nonperforming first-lien mortgages secured by skilled-nursing and assisted-living facilities in nine states. The loans will be sold without Federal Housing Administration insurance and with servicing released; qualified bidders may bid on pools organized by characteristics such as property type and performance. Bids are scheduled for November 17, with closing around December 9. The notice exposes one mechanism by which the government exits distressed healthcare real-estate credit.

items.title: Treasury consolidates sanctions-penalty procedures into a common rulebook
items.summary: The Office of Foreign Assets Control creates a single sanctions-penalties part covering programs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and United Nations Participation Act. OFAC says the rule changes no substantive penalty provisions; it gathers investigation rights, notices, settlement, findings, collection, and disclosure rules now repeated across separate programs. International Emergency Economic Powers Act civil exposure remains the greater of $377,700 or twice a transaction’s value, while voluntary self-disclosure generally halves the base penalty.

items.title: Eli Lilly seeks foreign-trade-zone treatment for a broad injectable-drug portfolio
items.summary: Eli Lilly notified the Foreign-Trade Zones Board of proposed production at its Concord, North Carolina, facility using foreign-status drug substances, devices, vials, needles, and syringes. The finished-product list spans incretin and amylin weight-management therapies, diabetes drugs, migraine and inflammatory-disease antibodies, and an amyloid-targeted Alzheimer’s therapy. Some inputs remain subject to Section 232 or 301 treatment and must enter in privileged foreign status. Comments close November 4.

items.title: Postal Service rewrites its remaining environmental-review procedures
items.summary: The Postal Service issued an interim final rule, with comments invited through October 26, that partially rescinds and updates its remaining procedures under the National Environmental Policy Act. USPS explains that the provisions had been written to implement Council on Environmental Quality regulations that have since been rescinded. The document is a concrete example of how a change in government-wide procedural architecture propagates into an independent establishment’s project-review rules.

items.title: NHTSA treats isolated failures in twenty-year-old vehicles as wear, not a fleet defect
items.summary: NHTSA denied a petition seeking a defect investigation of model-year 2006 Nissan Frontiers for alleged fuel leaks and engine stalling. Its Office of Defects Investigation found no fleetwide trend and distinguished the symptoms from three earlier recalls involving other platforms or different failure mechanisms. The agency emphasized vehicle age, mileage, failure frequency, and the difference between inherent design defects and ordinary component degradation. The determination illustrates the evidentiary threshold for opening a federal safety investigation.

items.title: Field report assesses pressure on Yemen’s Taiz–Aden route and reduced Israeli forces in Lebanon
items.publisher: Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project
items.summary: The Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project assess that Yemeni government-aligned forces repelled a Houthi attempt to cut the principal Taiz–Aden supply route on September 23. The report also says Israel reduced its southern-Lebanon ground presence from eight brigades to six after recent operations. Both are analytical judgments assembled from official, local, media, and geolocated sources; the report expressly distinguishes observed movements, reported claims, and its own inferences.

items.title: NIH proposes requiring plain-language study results to be returned to participants
items.summary: NIH’s draft policy would require all NIH-supported clinical research to offer participants plain-language summaries of aggregate results, unless an institute approves an exception. Clinical-trial summaries would generally be due within one year of primary completion or by the applicable ClinicalTrials.gov deadline, whichever is later; other studies receive different schedules and status-update duties. Compliance would become an award condition, with possible funding consequences. NIH seeks comment on participant preferences, research burdens, costs, and implementation tools.
items.source_type: Draft policy and request for information

items.title: FDA drafts a common testing framework for robotically assisted surgical devices
items.summary: FDA released draft recommendations for the nonclinical testing, clinical testing, and submission content of robotically assisted surgical devices. The agency defines these as teleoperated, software-controlled systems that help practitioners position and control multiple instruments during open, minimally invasive, or endoluminal procedures. FDA says the guidance is intended to make premarket reviews more consistent and efficient; it is not final, binding, or ready for implementation. Comments are requested by November 24.

items.title: FDA panel will review low-dose atropine intended to slow childhood myopia
items.summary: FDA’s Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee will meet October 30 to consider Sydnexis’s application for atropine sulfate ophthalmic solution at 0.01 percent, proposed to slow myopia progression in children aged three or older. The notice announces an open public meeting rather than an approval or efficacy finding. Background materials and comments will enter a public docket, with comments received by October 19 supplied to the committee and the docket closing October 29.

items.title: NOAA closes the September commercial bluefin fishery as its subquota nears exhaustion
items.summary: The National Marine Fisheries Service closed the General-category Atlantic bluefin tuna fishery at 11:30 p.m. on September 24 after reported landings indicated that September’s 216.1-metric-ton subquota would soon be reached. Retention and landing of bluefin at least 73 inches long are barred through September 30, though permitted vessels may tag and release fish under handling rules. The fishery reopens automatically October 1, when scheduled restricted-fishing days resume.
